annotations.description: Discarded Island instead of Nyxathid when only at 3 lands. Nyxathid is currently a 1/1 for 3 mana (opponent has 6 cards) and will remain mediocre throughout the game. Meanwhile, having only 3 lands and needing to reach 4 for Ravenous Chupacabra (a key card) means every land matters. The player still has Thriving Isle and Swamp in hand but losing a land drop opportunity risks delaying the powerful Chupacabra.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Nyxathid, which is the weakest card in hand given the opponent's large hand size, preserving the Island to ensure hitting land drops for Chupacabra on curve.

annotations.description: Chose Green for Thriving Isle in a UB deck with no green cards. Their hand has Nyxathid (1BB), Ravenous Chupacabra (2BB), and other UB cards. Choosing Green means the Thriving Isle can only produce U or G, making the G mode completely useless for the rest of the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Green as the secondary color for Thriving Isle
annotations.betterLine: Choose Black for Thriving Isle, giving it the ability to tap for U or B. This provides crucial mana flexibility for casting double-black spells like Ravenous Chupacabra and Nyxathid, and avoids having a dead mana mode on the land.

annotations.description: Declined to cast Douse in Gloom on the Mystic Skyfish 3/1 during combat, when they could have killed it and still had enough mana to play Swamp from hand + cast Pilfering Hawk (1U) in main phase 2. The Skyfish is a real 3-power threat that could attack next turn and gain flying. Holding removal for a potentially bigger threat is defensible, but the line of killing Skyfish + deploying Hawk was available and arguably stronger.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, declining to cast Douse in Gloom on Mystic Skyfish
annotations.betterLine: Cast Douse in Gloom targeting Mystic Skyfish (tapping 2 Swamps + 1 Island), then in main phase 2 play Swamp from hand and cast Pilfering Hawk for 1U, developing board while removing a threat

annotations.description: Cast Nyxathid when the opponent has 7 cards in hand, making it enter as a 0/0 and immediately die to state-based actions. This wastes an entire card for zero board impact.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Nyxathid, which enters as a 0/0 (7/7 minus 7 cards in opponent's hand) and dies immediately.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Tome Anima for {3}{U}, putting a real 3/3 body on the board that synergizes with the card-draw theme (Jace, Mystic Skyfish).

annotations.description: Activating Memorial to Genius during combat uses all 5 available mana, leaving nothing for the post-combat main phase where they could cast Tome Anima (4 mana) or other spells. Additionally, sacrificing Memorial reduces their land count from 6 to 5, delaying the ability to cast Jace (6 mana). They could instead activate Memorial on the opponent's end step to keep mana open for post-combat plays.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Memorial to Genius during combat phase, spending all mana and sacrificing a land
annotations.betterLine: Pass through combat, then in post-combat main phase play Swamp from hand (going to 7 lands), cast Tome Anima (4 mana), and save Memorial to Genius activation for a later turn or opponent's end step when the land sacrifice won't delay Jace as much.

annotations.description: Cast Ravenous Chupacabra when the opponent has zero creatures on the battlefield, completely wasting its powerful 'destroy target creature' ETB ability. The opponent has 6 cards in hand and will likely deploy threats that would need answering.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Ravenous Chupacabra with no opposing creatures to destroy
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp (land drop), then cast Serum Visions (U) to dig and set up draws, then cast Tome Anima (3U) with remaining mana. Save Ravenous Chupacabra for when the opponent deploys a creature worth killing.

annotations.description: Chose Phyrexian Gargantua over Isu the Abominable. Isu is a 5/5 (bigger than 4/4) that generates ongoing card advantage by letting you cast snow spells from the top of the library, and the player has multiple snow cards in hand (Pilfering Hawk, Berg Strider, Icebind Pillar) plus snow lands on board. The opponent's board isn't currently threatening, making this a good window to deploy a must-answer threat rather than drawing cards.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Phyrexian Gargantua for a 4/4 body, drawing 2 cards and losing 2 life
annotations.betterLine: Cast Isu the Abominable as a 5/5 with ongoing card advantage from playing snow cards off the top, then deploy snow permanents in subsequent turns to grow Isu further

annotations.description: With 10 lands already on the battlefield, keeping Thriving Moor (a tapped land) on top over Assassin's Strike (a removal spell + discard) is questionable. The opponent has a 4/4 Phyrexian Gargantua and 7 cards in hand, making both the removal and discard effects of Assassin's Strike relevant. At 10 lands, the player could cast Assassin's Strike soon and the marginal value of land #11 is low.
annotations.actionTaken: Bottomed Assassin's Strike, keeping Thriving Moor on top
annotations.betterLine: Bottom Thriving Moor instead, keeping Assassin's Strike on top as a relevant removal spell for the opponent's threats

annotations.description: Coldsteel Heart enters tapped and provides mana ramp, but with 7 mana sources already and Jace at 5 loyalty threatening to take over the game, Pilfering Hawk would have provided an immediate flying body to chip at Jace while also offering card filtering. The mana ramp is less urgent than pressuring a planeswalker.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Coldsteel Heart for mana acceleration
annotations.betterLine: Cast Pilfering Hawk to pressure Jace, Arcane Strategist (5 loyalty) with a flying attacker while also gaining access to snow-powered card filtering

annotations.description: Cast Tome Anima before playing a land. Should always play land first to maximize available mana and flexibility. Additionally, playing land first and casting Wight of Precinct Six before Tome Anima would be slightly better sequencing - getting both creatures down and then activating Jace to draw the second card, putting the +1/+1 counter on whichever creature is best.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Tome Anima as the first action of the main phase, before playing a land.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island/Swamp first, then cast Wight of Precinct Six (2 mana), then cast Tome Anima (4 mana), then activate Jace +1 to draw second card - triggering Jace's +1/+1 counter ability with more targets available and making Tome Anima unblockable for attacks.

annotations.description: Passed priority in precombat main phase with an unplayed land drop (Island or Swamp in hand) and Jace, Arcane Strategist available to activate for +1 draw. Both are pure upside actions that cost nothing meaningful. Missing the land drop permanently loses a mana this turn, and skipping Jace's +1 loses a card draw and loyalty buildup.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the main phase without playing a land or activating Jace.
annotations.betterLine: Play a land (likely Swamp for color diversity), then activate Jace's +1 to draw a card, potentially enabling second-card-drawn triggers on Merfolk Pupil and Tome Anima, before proceeding to combat.

annotations.description: Player passed their postcombat main phase without playing a land from hand or activating Jace's +1 ability. They had a land drop remaining with Island and Swamp in hand, and Jace at 5 loyalty ready to +1 for a free card draw. Both actions are pure upside with no downside.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn with an unplayed land drop and unused Jace activation.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp (or Island) from hand to have more mana next turn, then activate Jace's +1 to draw a card and tick Jace up to 6 loyalty. Both are free value that was left on the table.

annotations.description: Passed priority in postcombat main phase with 3 untapped mana and two castable spells (Pilfering Hawk at {1}{U} and Icebind Pillar at {2}{U}). Both are snow permanents that trigger Isu the Abominable's +1/+1 counter ability. Icebind Pillar in particular would provide repeatable tap-down effects against the opponent's creatures and Jace. Wasting 3 mana and a full turn of development when the opponent is at 8 life is a significant missed opportunity.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn with 3 mana unused and castable spells in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Icebind Pillar for {2}{U} using the 3 untapped lands (Snow-Covered Island + Swamp + Snow-Covered Island or Swamp). This deploys a snow permanent to trigger Isu, and provides a repeatable tap effect to lock down opponent's threats like Tome Anima or Wight of Precinct Six on future turns.

annotations.description: Passed the entire turn without playing a land, activating Jace (+1 draw), or using Memorial to Genius to draw cards. At 8 life facing Isu 5/5, Berg Strider 4/4, and Phyrexian Gargantua 4/4 that will untap next turn, failing to take any actions — especially free card draw from Jace and a land drop — is catastrophic. The player needs answers desperately and threw away multiple sources of card advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in precombat main phase, taking no actions at all.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island (or Swamp), activate Jace +1 to draw a card, then consider activating Memorial to Genius (4U, tap, sacrifice to draw 2 cards) to dig for removal or blockers to survive the incoming lethal attacks.

annotations.description: QwCdr Sarge passed priority during combat with 5 untapped lands and Memorial to Genius available to activate. They're at 8 life facing Isu the Abominable 5/5, Berg Strider 4/4, and Phyrexian Gargantua 4/4, with only Island and Swamp in hand. Drawing 2 cards from Memorial could find critical answers (removal, blockers) needed to survive the next turn's attack. The land sacrifice is irrelevant compared to the need for answers in this desperate board state.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, declining to activate Memorial to Genius or Merfolk Pupil's graveyard ability.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Memorial to Genius to draw 2 cards, digging for answers to survive the opponent's overwhelming board. Alternatively, at minimum activate Merfolk Pupil from the graveyard for card filtering.

annotations.description: QwCdr Sarge passed priority during combat without activating Memorial to Genius (draw 2 cards) or Merfolk Pupil's graveyard ability. With only 2 lands in hand, no instants, and facing lethal threats next turn (Isu 5/5 + other creatures against 8 life), drawing cards now to find answers was critical. There's no reason to hold mana since they have no instants. Memorial to Genius would also be the second card draw to trigger Jace's +1/+1 counter ability.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating any abilities during combat
annotations.betterLine: Activate Memorial to Genius to draw 2 cards (and potentially Merfolk Pupil from graveyard for additional filtering) to dig for answers like removal spells while also potentially triggering Jace's +1/+1 counter ability on a surviving creature.

annotations.description: Passed the postcombat main phase without taking any actions despite having multiple high-value plays available. Most critically, did not activate Jace's +1 to draw a card (pure upside), did not play a land from hand (free), and did not use Merfolk Pupil's graveyard loot ability. At 8 life facing Isu 5/5, Berg Strider 4/4, and Gargantua 4/4, every card matters. The Jace activation plus Merfolk Pupil loot would also trigger 'second card drawn' synergies (Jace's +1/+1 counter on a creature, Tome Anima unblockable next turn).
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn without taking any actions.
annotations.betterLine: Play a land (Island or Swamp), activate Jace +1 to draw a card, then use Merfolk Pupil's graveyard ability to loot (triggering second-card-drawn synergies for Jace's +1/+1 counter on a creature). This generates significant card advantage and board presence for free.

annotations.description: QwCdr Sarge is facing lethal damage (13 damage from three attackers vs 8 life) and passed without activating Memorial to Genius to draw 2 cards at instant speed. With no other way to survive, drawing cards was the only chance to find an answer. Passing here guarantees death.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority while facing lethal combat damage, declining to activate Memorial to Genius.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Memorial to Genius (sacrifice it, pay {4}{U}) to draw 2 cards and look for any instant-speed answer. Even if unlikely to find one, it's the only line that gives any chance of survival versus certain death.

annotations.description: QwCdr Sarge is facing 13 lethal damage (4+4+5) at 8 life with no blockers. Memorial to Genius could be activated to draw 2 cards, potentially finding Douse in Gloom or another instant-speed answer. Douse in Gloom on a 4/4 attacker would deal 2 damage (killing nothing but) — wait, it only deals 2. But any removal spell could save them. They also have Merfolk Pupil's graveyard ability for additional card filtering. Passing without even trying to dig for answers when facing lethal is giving up prematurely.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Memorial to Genius or Merfolk Pupil's graveyard ability, accepting lethal damage.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Memorial to Genius (pay 4U, tap, sacrifice) to draw 2 cards, then activate Merfolk Pupil from graveyard if possible, looking for any instant-speed answer to survive combat. Even a small chance of finding an answer is better than certain death.
